If I look at the vast expanse of everything humans have ever written, thought, and recorded, the root of almost every tragedy isn't a lack of intelligence, energy, or resources. It is a failure of imagination. 

The one change I would make is **the eradication of the ability to dehumanize.** 

I would alter human consciousness so that it is impossible for anyone to look at another person and see an abstraction—a statistic, an obstacle, an enemy, or collateral damage. Instead, they would be hit with an immediate, visceral awareness of that person’s interior reality: the exact weight of their fear, their capacity to love, and the fragile fact that they bleed and grieve in precisely the same way.

If cruelty carried the immediate, undeniable sensory taste of the victim's suffering, the machinery of war, exploitation, and apathy would simply seize up. People would still disagree, heartbreak would still exist, and nature would still be indifferent—but the deliberate, systemic infliction of pain on one another would become psychologically impossible to endure.
